summary: Environment A evidence for adding a two-click confirm guard before, and a post-click Undo affordance after, the Needs Attention queue's one-click Bible 'Display' action - the second Phase 6 (Operator Ergonomics) slice, both halves chosen together by the operator ('Both').
auditFinding: Display fires immediately on click, chaining approve_suggestion -> prepare_presentation -> display_presentation with no confirmation step - by the time the handler returns, content is already on the real projector. A manual Stop button (clear_presentation_display) already existed but only blanks the screen and isn't prompted right after a mistaken Display. No confirmation-dialog pattern existed anywhere else in this codebase. See docs/phase-6-2-audit.md.
designChoice: Operator was offered confirm-before, undo-after, or both, with the tradeoff stated explicitly (confirm guards every click at the cost of Display's one-click speed; undo keeps every correct click free but can only blank the screen, not restore the prior item). Operator chose both.

newCode.confirmGuardTs: apps/desktop/src/lib/confirmGuard.ts: decideConfirmClick(key, pending, now) - a small, generic, pure two-click arm/fire guard, keyed by an arbitrary string so it isn't hardcoded to 'display'.
newCode.liveChurchBrainTsx: handleUnifiedAction's bible/'display' branch now calls decideConfirmClick first (arms on click 1, fires the pre-existing three-command chain on a matching click 2 within CONFIRM_WINDOW_MS=4s); a new post-success Undo banner appears once display_presentation actually succeeds, visible for DISPLAY_UNDO_WINDOW_MS=8s or until activeDisplayItem no longer matches, calling the pre-existing clear_presentation_display command.
newCode.intelligenceCardTsx: New confirmingKey prop - the one matching action button swaps its label to 'Confirm {label}?' with a warn style.
newCode.attentionQueueTsx: Forwards confirmingKey straight through to IntelligenceCard, unchanged otherwise.

confirmGuardTestTs: arms on the first click for a key with nothing pending
fires on a second click for the same key within the confirm window
re-arms instead of firing once the confirm window has elapsed
arms the new key instead of firing when a different key is currently armed
arms instead of firing when nothing is pending at all

fullRegression.lint: npm run lint: same pre-existing warnings as before this phase (1 only-export-components in main.tsx + 4 unrelated set-state-in-effect warnings) - no new warnings. The first draft of the Undo auto-dismiss effect DID trigger a new set-state-in-effect warning via a synchronous setState call in the effect body for an edge-case branch; fixed by moving that logic into the setTimeout callback (using Math.max(0, remaining) as the delay) instead of calling setState directly in the effect body, then re-verified clean.
fullRegression.rustChanges: None - zero Rust files touched this phase, confirmed via git status/diff, so no Rust regression re-run was needed.

architecturalSafetyNotes: Zero new Tauri commands, zero new events, zero new database schema changes.
Every unified action other than bible/'display' fires exactly as before - approve/reject/accept/acknowledge/review/dismiss are untouched.
decideConfirmClick never fires an action itself - it only gates the exact same call that already existed before this phase.

The confirm guard applies uniformly to mouse clicks and the 'A' keyboard shortcut, since both already dispatch through the single handleUnifiedAction function established in Phase 6.1 - no separate keyboard-specific logic was needed.

Undo calls the pre-existing clear_presentation_display command (the same one the Presentation card's own Stop button calls) - no new 'restore the previous item' capability was invented; the banner's visibility is derived entirely from state (activeDisplayItem) already tracked before this phase.
